mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last two weeks (-45.1 to -37.6), indicating positive momentum in retail footfall recovery that is expected to continue as consumer habits re-normalize, producing a higher 4-week mean than the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -45.1 at t-2w to -37.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the trailing 4-week mean despite the recent upward trend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-over-week acceleration in PARKS mobility (34.9 to 25.1 percent deficit, a 9.8-point jump) signals growing public comfort with outdoor and public-facing activity, which should spill over into retail visitation within two weeks as behavioral norms loosen broadly.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change exceeds +5 points for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -33.4 at t-1w to -25.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over the subsequent 2 weeks despite PARKS crossing the +5 point weekly threshold, the spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT (-74.7 to -73.0) and WORKPLACES (-34.9 to -33.0) jointly indicate loosening of mobility restrictions or policy relaxation, which together amplify retail recovery more than either series alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show simultaneous week-on-week improvement for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved monotonically across the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 4 weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved jointly for 2+ weeks, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for three consecutive weeks (19.3 to 18.0), indicating people are spending relatively less time at home, which behaviorally frees up time for near-term retail and recreation trips within the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.1 at t-2w to 18.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the immediate next week despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS increase may reflect seasonal warming driving outdoor recreational substitution away from indoor retail and recreation venues, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks as time is reallocated to parks rather than shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved by 9.8 points in the most recent week, outpacing RETAIL_REC's 5.5-point gain
regime_hint: seasonal warming period with reopening underway
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise in step with or faster than PARKS over the next 2 weeks, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is approaching its pre-period baseline (-1.0 at t-0w), suggesting that the easiest, most essential mobility recovery has largely been captured; once this series saturates near zero, overall mobility recovery momentum (including RETAIL_REC) tends to decelerate in the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -2 points (near baseline saturation)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -2.4 at t-1w to -1.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise at the same or faster rate in the week after GROCERY_PHARM crosses -2 points, the saturation-deceleration hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A compound easing regime defined by rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility combined with falling RESIDENTIAL mobility jointly signals a coordinated policy-driven return to normal activity patterns, which together should drive a stronger and more durable 4-week increase in RETAIL_REC than any single series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week, for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved while RESIDENTIAL declined across the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not exceed the trailing 4-week mean despite this joint 3-series pattern persisting, the compound-regime hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility, despite remaining deeply suppressed (-73.0), is slowly and consistently improving week over week; this persistent incremental recovery in transit usage is a leading behavioral indicator that commuting and errand-based trips (including retail) will keep rising over the next week regardless of regime.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved monotonically from -74.7 to -73.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the immediate next week despite TRANSIT's continued monotonic improvement, the leading-indicator hypothesis is rejected.
